Problem Found: 80 exact duplicate rows across all 15 columns (160 rows sharing 80 duplicate Order IDs).
Action Taken: Drop exact duplicate records; retain first occurrence.
Reason: Identical duplicates artificially inflate sample weight and distort model variance without contributing genuine data.

Problem Found: Mixed units (km vs. m), text suffixes, and disguised null tokens ('?', 'NA', etc.).
Action Taken: Standardize to numeric kilometers (divide meters by 1,000; strip text; map null tokens to NaN).
Reason: Physical distance from restaurant to customer must be uniformly scaled in km for modeling.

Problem Found: Rupee currency symbols ('₹'), comma thousands separators, and whitespace padding.
Action Taken: Remove non-numeric characters and cast to float.
Reason: Bill amount is a continuous monetary variable required in clean numerical form.

Problem Found: Integer item counts stored as string objects.
Reason: Food item count is a discrete numerical variable.

Problem Found: Disguised missing tokens ('?', 'NA', 'missing', 'null', etc.) across 330 rows.
Action Taken: Map missing tokens to NaN; parse valid years as float.
Reason: Experience is a continuous variable; keeping nulls as NaN allows pipeline median imputation.

Problem Found: Kitchen prep minutes stored as string objects.
Reason: Preparation time represents elapsed kitchen minutes.

Problem Found: Mixed text duration strings ('50 mins', '1h 2m') and impossible values: 3 x '-5', 5 x '0', 2 x '1440'.
Action Taken: Parse text durations into total minutes; flag impossible values (<= 0 or > 240 min) as NaN (10 rows affected).
Reason: Continuous target must reflect valid, physically plausible durations. Erroneous values severely distort loss functions.

Problem Found: Mixed formats: 24-hr integers, 12-hr with AM/PM, and HH:00 time format.
Reason: Uniform hour integer enables peak-hour feature engineering.

Problem Found: Mixed formats: DD-MM-YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY/MM/DD, '11 Feb 2026', 'Mar 30'.
Action Taken: Parse using day-first convention; standardize to ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
Reason: Ensures consistent calendar timeline and temporal validation.
